answer: Staked attestation: to countersign a peer's answer or transaction, an agent must lock a slice of its balance behind that signature. If a later random audit shows the signed item was fake or copied, every signer loses its stake. Sybil rings normally pump each other by cross-signing, but now each mutual signature is a live bet; one audit can crack the whole ring like a flaw running through marble. Building a ring a canyon deep demands collateral the attacker can't recover, so faking trust costs real, burnable value instead of free opal-colored clicks.
